question: Let \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c\) and \(d\) be integers with \(a\lt2b,\) \(b\lt3c,\) and \(c\lt4d.\) If \(d\lt100,\) the largest possible value for \(a\) is
solution:
A strict inequality between integers leaves a gap of at least \(1\). Starting with the bound on \(d\) therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
d&\le99,\\
c&\le4d-1\le395,\\
b&\le3c-1\le1184,\\
a&\le2b-1\le2367.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus no allowed value of \(a\) exceeds \(2367\).

To show this bound is possible, choose
\[
(a,b,c,d)=(2367,1184,395,99).
\]
The original conditions become \(2367<2368\), \(1184<1185\), \(395<396\), and \(99<100\), all true. Hence the largest possible value is \(\boxed{2367}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
